title: A room ban removes nobody: the banned member keeps reading the room and returns through an invite its owners cannot revoke

steps.action: while still a moderator, mint an invite with days 0 and maxUses 0, then let the room's owner try to list and revoke it
steps.result: a permanent, unlimited way into the private room that the room's own owner can neither see nor revoke (listInvites and removeInvite both answer HTTP 403)

steps.action: after the ban, keep the banned account's own notification stream open and fetch the room's upload by its id
steps.result: every message posted in the room after the ban, in real time, and the confidential file, while the room's history and message stream correctly refuse the same account

steps.action: set the room's desktop, email and mobile notification level to all through rooms.saveNotification, whose only gate is the same subscription lookup the ban does not filter
steps.result: accepted with HTTP 200 for a banned member, so the leak of step 2 is turned up from mentions to every message

steps.action: register a new account through the public form and redeem the invite from step 1 (the banned account's own redemption is correctly refused with user is banned from this room)
steps.result: a member of the private group again under a new identity, reading the whole history including the message posted after the ban

combined_impact: Proven in the lab: after a ban that the product applied correctly at the front door, the banned person kept receiving the room's new messages and downloaded its confidential file, raised the room's notification level so nothing would be missed, and walked back in under a new account through an invite the room's owners could not take away. Attacker capability before the ban: a moderator of the room. After the ban, which is supposed to remove them entirely: real-time reading, file access, and full membership again. The blast radius is every private room whose moderation relies on the ban, and the people in it who believe the room was closed to that person. The documentation this contradicts is the product's own: a banned user cannot re-enter the room through any path (docs/features/ban-user.md).
preconditions: The attacker was a member of the room with the ability to create an invite (a moderator, which any user becomes in a room they create), and public self-registration is on, which is the shipped default. No setting is changed.
fix_order: Fix step 1 and step 4 together at one place: re-validate the invite's creator and the redeeming account in useInviteToken (useInviteToken.ts:10-69, VULN-035), so an invite minted by someone who has since lost their standing in the room stops admitting anybody, and scope the create-invite-links check in listInvites and removeInvite to the room so the room's owners can revoke what exists. That single change closes re-entry, which is the part of the chain that restores full membership. Side effect: keeps the feature and removes only the weakness: live invites from current members keep working, while invites created by members who have been removed, demoted or banned stop working, which will surprise rooms that rely on an old link; the notification and file-path leaks (VULN-009) need their own fix, filtering banned subscriptions in the recipient query and in the file access check, because they continue regardless of the invite.
